verdict.basis: The assertion covers IIA "Greece" agricultural data for 1919-1945 (24 years, 250 rows), fully inside candidate GRC-1919-1947 (1919-1947). The wiki page (draft) documents a specific, checkable territorial claim: Treaty of Neuilly (1919) fixed the western/Bulgarian border and added Western Thrace; the polygon (CShapes 2.0, cowcode=350, 1919-11-27 feature, ~129,479 km²) explicitly excludes the Dodecanese (still Italian, ITAEG) until the 1947 Paris Peace Treaty cession — the event that ends this row. Since the observed span (1919-1945) ends two years before that 1947 boundary change, the reporting territory is constant across the whole observed span; no annexation/cession/occupation-driven territorial redefinition falls inside 1919-1945 (WWII 1941-44 Axis occupation is administrative, not a change to the recognised state's territorial scope, consistent with WHEP convention). Staple magnitudes (wine ~155k t, raisins ~155k t, cotton lint ~24k ha) are plausible in scale for interwar Greek agriculture (a major raisin/currant exporter) and don't show a discontinuity vs. the neighboring pre-1919 segments (GRC-1881-1913, GRC-1913-1919), supporting territorial continuity rather than a scope jump. The specific treaty-based claims (Neuilly 1919, Lausanne 1923, Dodecanese 1947) are independently verifiable historical facts, not just the page's say-so, so this is not purely circular reliance on the draft.

review.basis: The assertion covers IIA 'greece' rows for 1919-1945, entirely inside candidate GRC-1919-1947's span (1919-1947); the observed data ends before the only documented territorial change in that row (the 1947 Dodecanese cession from Italy), so no split is needed within the observed years. Greece was not part of any political union in this era (ruling out union/empire-scope confusion), had no colonial territory to conflate with metropolitan reporting, and the WWII Axis occupation (1941-1944) did not alter the recognised state's boundaries, so occupation-era rows should not be rerouted. The candidate's draft wiki page documents the territory (excludes Dodecanese, includes Western Thrace acquired at Neuilly 1919, matching the data's start year) but I do not rely on it alone: the neighbouring segments (1911-1913 -> GRC-1881-1913, 1914-1918 -> GRC-1913-1919) show the same ISO-based routing scheme used consistently across adjacent periods with no indicated territorial discontinuity at the 1919 boundary, and the reported staple magnitudes (e.g. raisins ~155,000t, wine ~155,000t, cotton seed ~20,000t) are plausible in scale for interwar Greece and show no internal break suggesting a mid-span scope change. Overall the source's reporting territory (the recognised Greek state, Western Thrace included, Dodecanese excluded) matches the candidate's territory for the entire 1919-1945 observed span.

verdict.basis: The assertion covers IIA agricultural-commodity data labeled 'malawi' (iso mwi) for 1909-1945, entirely within Nyasaland's 1891-1953 protectorate period, a span during which the territory (present-day Malawi) was fixed by the 1891 Anglo-Portuguese treaty and unchanged (per CShapes 2.0 exact historical polygon, gwcode 553). Staple magnitudes (cotton lint ~1,100 ha median, tobacco ~3,600 ha, tea ~2,000 ha, coffee ~140 ha) are plausible for Nyasaland's small colonial smallholder/estate agricultural economy and show no evidence of a scale discontinuity suggesting a broader or narrower reporting territory. No union/combined-reporting risk applies here (unlike Sweden-Norway or Yemen cases) since Nyasaland was a standalone protectorate, not merged into a larger federation until 1953, after the observed span ends in 1945. The wiki page is draft status, so its territorial narrative is treated as an unverified hypothesis, but the core claim -- constant Nyasaland/Malawi territory 1891-1953 -- is independently corroborated by CShapes 2.0 being an exact historical polygon source (not a proxy) and by the plausibility of the magnitudes; no external contradiction was found.

Candidate FCM-1920-1960 = French Cameroon (League mandate 1920-46, UN trust 1946-60, French-administered), CShapes cowcode 471, area 423,069 km². The Mitchell "cameroon"/iso=cmr series for 1920-1959 (308 rows, cacao/coffee/cattle/maize/groundnuts) sits between neighbor segments routed to GKM (German Kamerun, pre-1916) and BCM (British occupation, 1916-1919) before partition, and to CMR-1960-1961 after independence — consistent with the historically documented 1922 Milner-Simon partition creating French vs British Cameroon zones. Web research (Britannica/colonial economic history) confirms cocoa was economically crucial to French Cameroun but of no real economic importance in the British Mandate zone, so a cacao/coffee-heavy "Cameroon" series of this magnitude in this period is almost certainly reporting French Cameroon alone, not a combined French+British figure — ruling out the combined-reporting failure mode. The territory (Milner-Simon partition line) stayed essentially constant 1920/1922-1959 aside from a minor 1931 Wouri-enclave adjustment noted on the wiki page and reflected in the single CShapes polygon (FID 354/355) covering the whole span, so this does not rise to the level of a mid-span annexation/cession that would force best_available. The wiki page is draft status and was explicitly authored to fill this same data gap (some circularity risk), but its core territorial claim (French mandate/trust zone, ~423,069 km², partitioned from German Kamerun in 1920-22) is independently corroborated by CShapes GIS record and general colonial history, not merely self-referential.
verdict.wiki_note: Independent corroboration for the "Data routing" rationale: colonial economic history (Britannica and cocoa-history literature) confirms cacao had no real economic importance in the British Cameroons mandate zone but was central to French Cameroun's economy — this supports that Mitchell's cacao/coffee-bearing "Cameroon" series for 1920-1959 is French Cameroon alone, not a combined French+British figure, which the current page does not address.

verdict.basis: The assertion covers Mitchell agricultural/livestock data (coffee, cattle, maize, goats, swine) labeled 'angola' for 1908-1960, routed to ANG-1905-1975 (Portuguese Angola, 1905-1975). The candidate's territory was fixed by the 1905 Victor Emmanuel III arbitration finalizing the SE frontier with Northern Rhodesia, and per the wiki (and general historical consensus on Portuguese Angola's colonial borders) remained unchanged through independence in 1975 — the observed span 1908-1960 falls entirely inside this stable-border window, well clear of both the 1905 boundary-fixing event and 1975 independence. The neighbor_segment for 1898-1903 correctly routes to the predecessor ANG-1891-1905, confirming the data source itself tracks the same 1905 border discontinuity our period split uses, i.e. no misalignment between source reporting basis and our splits. Mitchell's country-level agricultural series for colonial Angola report the whole Portuguese colony (no known combined-reporting issue analogous to French Algeria/Sweden-Norway for this label), and the magnitudes (e.g. ~18,000t coffee, ~1.17M cattle, 300,000t maize) are plausible in scale for a colony the size of Angola, not for some smaller sub-territory. The wiki page is draft and its territorial narrative is the primary basis, but it is corroborated by (a) the magnitude plausibility, (b) the neighbor-segment consistency with the 1905 border event, and (c) the specific, checkable historical claim (1891 Anglo-Portuguese Treaty / 1905 arbitration) which matches standard colonial-Angola historiography, so I am not relying on the draft page alone.

review.basis: The assertion covers Mitchell's 'Angola' production series 1908-1960, routed to ANG-1905-1975 (Portuguese Angola, borders fixed by the 1905 Victor Emmanuel arbitration and unchanged through independence in 1975 per CShapes 2.0). The observed span (1908-1960) sits entirely within this stable-border window, well clear of the 1905 boundary change (whose pre-1905 side is correctly routed to a different candidate, ANG-1891-1905, per the neighbor_segments field). Mitchell's African Historical Statistics compiles colonial-territory series (Portuguese Angola as a single administrative unit), consistent with a smooth single-polity series here. Staple magnitudes (coffee ~18k tonnes, cattle ~1.17M head, maize ~300k tonnes) are plausible, non-discontinuous figures for a mid-20th-century colonial Angola and show no sign of a scope break across the 1908-1960 span. No combined-reporting or union-scope risk applies (Angola was administered directly as a single Portuguese colony, not part of a multi-territory federation in this period). The wiki page (draft status) documents the stable-border claim but I corroborate it via the neighbor-segment discontinuity pattern and general knowledge of Mitchell's compilation practice and Angola's colonial administrative history, not by taking the draft at face value alone.

verdict.basis: The assertion covers IIA agricultural yearbook data labeled 'canada' for 1909-1945, routed to CAN-1886-1948 (1886-1948, CShapes 2.0 polygon, ~9.55M km2, excluding Newfoundland which remained a separate Dominion until 1949). The observed span (1909-1945) falls entirely within a period the wiki documents as territorially stable — no annexations, cessions, or occupations affecting Canada's mainland/provincial territory during this window (Alberta/Saskatchewan creation in 1905 was an internal administrative reorganization, not a territorial change, and predates the observed span; Statute of Westminster 1931 was constitutional, not territorial). Staple magnitudes (eggs ~146,040 t median, sugar refined ~45,114 t median) are plausible for a country of Canada's agricultural scale and show no discontinuity suggesting a scope change. The wiki page, while draft status, gives a specific and internally consistent territorial account (CShapes 1886 polygon, Newfoundland excluded) that is corroborated by well-known historical fact (Newfoundland joined Canada only in 1949) independent of the page itself. No indication IIA 'Canada' data ever included Newfoundland separately as part of Canadian totals in this period. Territory equals candidate's and was constant across the whole span, so verified_equal applies.
